craft_claim: Baby-schema features trigger a cuteness and caretaking response at a perceptual level independent of comprehension, so a voice can satisfy the cute response while giving the reader nothing to imagine into.

supporting_evidence.note: Glocker et al. experimentally manipulated baby-schema content in infant faces and found high baby-schema faces rated cuter and eliciting stronger caretaking motivation; the concept traces to Lorenz (1943) and operates as a perceptual releaser, not a reasoning judgement.

counterevidence.note: Genuine nonsense requires meaningful elements alongside the nonsense, so cuteness that carries no imaginable prop fails the genre's own balance condition.

scope: Failure mode: cute surface without an imaginable prop, named in the taxonomy as 'cuteness without meaning'.
exceptions: Cuteness is not itself a fault; it fails only when it substitutes for a prop the reader can imagine into.
